text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. This gives us a clean baseline to measure its impact without disrupting active work. The trade-off is delayed visibility into open PRs, but we avoid noise in the review queue while validating accuracy. Once the merged PR confirms no false positives, we expand to open PRs.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs trains reviewers to ignore real issues because the model’s feedback arrives after the fact—when fixes are already merged. Better: run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first; this catches edge cases before they’re buried in history. Settle it by comparing false negative rates between open and merged PRs over two weeks.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* open and merged PRs from day one—this catches edge cases before they’re buried in history and avoids the false negative trap of waiting for merged PRs. The upfront cost of reviewing two streams of feedback is offset by faster, more reliable improvements.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first, then expand to merged PRs after a week. This catches edge cases before they’re buried in history and avoids the false negative trap of waiting for merged PRs. The trade-off is extra review noise upfront, but we avoid the bigger cost of retrofitting fixes later.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs first for one week, then expand to merged PRs—this catches edge cases early while minimizing retrofitting costs. Own it: Overhaul.
